Hi Priya / Anil —

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate you carving out time. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed: 

1) SOC 2 status: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type II certified (report available). Will attach the redacted report and a summary of controls related to data retention and deletion.

2) Data deletion SLAs: You asked about guaranteed deletion timelines for customer data and backups. Standard hosted offering: primary model request data + short-term logs are deleted from hot stores within 30 days by default; customer-configurable retention down to 0 days for request/response artifacts. Backups (snapshots) are retained for 90 days by default, with options for longer retention under Dedicated/Private contracts.

3) Log retention & backups: Audit logs necessary for debugging are retained for 7 days in hot storage and 365 days archived (encrypted) by default. Backups are encrypted, geo-redundant, and snapshot retention policies are separate from primary data retention. We flagged an action item to confirm how deletion is handled for backup snapshots that may include customer data.

4) GDPR/HIPAA: Redwood supports GDPR compliance (DPA available) and offers business associate agreement (BAA) for HIPAA-covered customers via our Private deployment or a Dedicated contract.

Hi Priya —

Thanks — great questions. Short answers below; happy to expand on a call with Security.

1) Hosted vs Dedicated/Private: In our standard hosted offering, backups are managed by Redwood as encrypted snapshots across cloud storage. We can support on-demand snapshot deletion requests, but full SLA-backed guarantees for physical snapshot purging within 30 days usually require a Dedicated contract (or Private deployment) because of how provider-level snapshots are handled and cross-tenant storage constraints. That said, we can offer documented procedures and evidence of deletion for hosted customers and may be able to negotiate tighter SLAs for named enterprise accounts with contractual commitments.

2) Logical vs physical deletion: For hosted snapshots, deletion is implemented as removal of snapshot metadata + lifecycle scheduling to purge object blocks; the underlying cloud provider ultimately handles block reclamation. For Dedicated/Private, we can provide stronger controls (dedicated storage) and more immediate physical purging.

3) KMS key lifecycle: Snapshot objects are encrypted with customer-specific keys in Dedicated/Private. In hosted, we use customer-scoped keys via Redwood-managed KMS or customer-managed keys (CMK) where available. When a snapshot is deleted, we rotate and retire any associated envelope keys; if a CMK is destroyed by customer request, access to snapshot objects becomes unrecoverable (we can provide controls and key-rotation proofs as required).

4) Proof of deletion: We can provide tamper-evident logs and a deletion certificate (hashes and timestamps) for deletion events. The certificate can be part of the evidence package for your audit.

- Priya: if you can send the VSQ to us, we’ll prioritize it and loop in Security.

A couple clarifications in writing so procurement/security has something to reference: 

- Hosted offering: default snapshot retention = 90 days. We can accept on-demand snapshot deletion requests; actual physical block reclamation timing depends on the underlying cloud provider (typically within 30-90 days after deletion request). We can provide deletion certificates within 48 hours of a deletion request.

- Dedicated/Private: for customers that require contractual SLAs for snapshot purge (e.g., 30 days), we recommend Dedicated or Private. Those options provide dedicated storage and stronger guarantees for immediate purging.

- KMS: Hosted supports customer-managed keys (CMK) in many regions; if Amaya elects CMK and requests key rotation/destruction, that can make deleted snapshots unrecoverable. We will include KMS key lifecycle controls and retention timelines in the VSQ response.
